Please summarize the following text in about five bullet points and then give it a suitable title.

Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they support roughly a quarter of all marine species. They are built over thousands of years by tiny animals called polyps, which secrete calcium carbonate skeletons and live in partnership with algae that provide them with energy through photosynthesis. When the water becomes too warm, the polyps expel the algae, causing the coral to turn white in a process known as bleaching. A bleached coral is not dead, but it is starved and vulnerable, and if the heat persists it will die. Mass bleaching events, once rare, have become more frequent as ocean temperatures rise. Scientists are experimenting with heat-tolerant coral strains, shading structures, and even assisted evolution to give reefs a chance. Local actions also matter: reducing agricultural runoff, controlling overfishing, and protecting mangroves that filter sediments can all make reefs more resilient. Still, researchers agree that without deep cuts to greenhouse gas emissions, even the best local efforts will not be enough to save most of the world's reefs. Tourism, which depends on healthy reefs in many tropical countries, is also at risk, and coastal communities that rely on reef fisheries and natural storm protection could face serious hardship.
